title: A Day at the Shipyard
description: While snapping pictures at a shipyard in Dhaka, Bangladesh, photographer GMB Akash could hear the “constant sound of hammering and metal work,” not unusual for a place where massive ships are repaired and constructed day in and day out. These workers—who earn around 1,000 taka per day (about 8 US dollars)—are docking this cargo ship by hand, which entails diving under the murky, polluted water below until the vessel is well-positioned and ready to reel in. This photo is featured in the "In Focus" series in the September 2026 issue of National Geographic.
translated_description: 在孟加拉国达卡的一家船厂拍摄照片时，摄影师GMB Akash能听到“持续的锤击声和金属作业声”，这对于一个日复一日维修和建造巨型船舶的地方来说并不稀奇。这些工人——每天收入约1000塔卡（约合8美元）——正用手工将这艘货船停靠入位，这需要潜入下方浑浊、污染的水中，直到船只定位妥当、准备就绪可以收缆。这张照片刊登在《国家地理》2026年9月号的“焦点”系列中。
